channel.title: PocketSurge
channel.description: Your daily dose of insights, guides, and reviews across technology, science, finance, gaming, and more.

item.title: RuneScape Housing Revamp Adds Build Mode and Neighborhoods
item.description: RuneScape's latest update revamps player housing with a flexible build mode and the ability to create neighborhoods with friends. Released on July 18, 2024, these features bring sandbox-level customization to the classic MMO. The update positions RuneScape at the forefront of a growing trend in MMO housing personalization.

item.title: LG to Ban Residential Proxy Networks from Smart TV Apps
item.description: LG will suspend smart TV apps acting as residential proxy nodes. With 42% of webOS apps containing proxy SDKs, this move addresses privacy violations and lack of informed consent. Developers must remove proxy features or face suspension.

item.title: Watching Too Much TV in Midlife May Shrink the Brain
item.description: Midlife TV binge-watching is linked to brain shrinkage, a new study finds. Sitting isn't the main culprit—the passivity of the activity is. Tech professionals must take note for long-term cognitive health.

item.title: When Listening to Music Was a Team Sport
item.description: An exploration of the Cooper Hewitt's 'Art of Noise' exhibition, revealing how jukeboxes and phonographs turned music listening into a shared, social 'team sport.' This stands in stark contrast to the isolated habits of modern streaming, and the article examines the design, culture, and quiet resurgence of communal listening.

item.title: Hello Sunshine: 10 Years of Big Little Lies, Lucky, Elle
item.description: As Hello Sunshine marks its 10th anniversary, Head of TV and Film Lauren Neustadter discusses Big Little Lies Season 3, Apple's Lucky, and Amazon's Elle. This article explores the company's impact on female-driven storytelling and the technology partnerships shaping content success.

item.title: Geologist Deaths in Movies: A Startling 34% Mortality Rate
item.description: A new study analyzing 141 movies spanning 1919 to 2023 reveals that fictional geologists die at an alarming rate, with a 34% mortality rate. The research highlights gender imbalance and genre patterns, offering fascinating insights into cinematic storytelling tropes.

item.title: Narwal Flow 2 Review: Perfecting Obstacle Avoidance and Mopping
item.description: The Narwal Flow 2 sets a new standard for robot vacuums with its exceptional obstacle avoidance and impressive mopping performance. It navigates furniture, cables, and small objects without hassle, and its smart mapping ensures efficient cleaning for technology professionals and enthusiasts.

item.title: Flipper Busy Bar Review: An Expensive Focus Tool Worth It?
item.description: The Flipper Busy Bar is an expensive productivity gadget that promises to protect your focus. Our review finds it doesn't stop interruptions but does help concentration through self-signaling. Here's our verdict for tech professionals.

item.title: Dyson V10 Konical Review (2026): Affordable and Solid
item.description: The Dyson V10 Konical delivers strong suction, solid runtime, and ergonomic design at a budget-friendly price. This review explores its performance, value, and why it's a standout choice in 2026's cordless vacuum market.

item.title: Whoopi Goldberg Defends Elliot Page's Casting in The Odyssey
item.description: Whoopi Goldberg defends Elliot Page's casting in 'The Odyssey' against transphobic critics, referencing the film's record-breaking $300M box office as proof that inclusive films succeed.

item.title: Yeon Sang-ho Returns to Parasyte Universe With 'Tamiya' on Netflix
item.description: Yeon Sang-ho returns to the Parasyte universe with a new live-action series 'Parasyte: Tamiya', starring Shioli Kutsuna and set for Netflix release in 2027. Co-written by Yeon and Ryu Yong-jae, the series continues Netflix's expansion of Korean originals and manga adaptations, showcasing cutting-edge VFX and global streaming technology.

item.title: The Odyssey's Key Visual: A 58-Year-Old Sci-Fi Inspiration
item.description: The Trojan horse sequence in The Odyssey draws direct cinematic lineage from Planet of the Apes. This analysis explores the technical and narrative artistry behind the inspiration, offering key lessons for tech professionals.

item.title: Spider-Man: Brand New Day Final Trailer Reveals New Villain
item.description: Sony has released the final trailer for Spider-Man: Brand New Day, unveiling an invisible threat and a new chapter for Peter Parker. The film, directed by Destin Daniel Cretton, launches a new trilogy. Here's a technical breakdown of the trailer and what fans can expect from the film's cutting-edge visual effects.

item.title: Clayface Trailer Leans Into Body Horror: A DCU Game-Changer
item.description: The debut Clayface trailer at San Diego Comic-Con signals a bold move into body horror for the DCU, with James Watkins directing and Alan Tudyk voicing Matt Hagen. This origin story promises to redefine superhero genre boundaries and showcase cutting-edge visual effects.

item.title: Antigravity Arcade: From prompt to game in minutes
item.description: Discover how Antigravity Arcade uses generative AI to transform text prompts into playable game prototypes in minutes, backed by data showing 55% studio adoption and 300% yearly growth in AI prototyping.

item.title: LTT's True 4K Gaming PC Build Guide (2026)
item.description: Discover the components and philosophy behind LTT's True 4K Gaming PC build for 2026. With a focus on smart pairing and real-world performance, this guide shows how to achieve 144+ FPS in AAA titles without overspending.

item.title: Neural-Signals: A Powerful C# Library for Neural Signal Processing and Time-Warping Analysis
item.description: Discover Neural-Signals, an open-source C# library that brings robust dynamic time warping and signal processing to .NET developers. Learn how this tool accelerates EEG and EMG analysis with up to 3x faster DTW computation and streamlined pipelines.

item.title: Neural Maze's Production OCR Course: Build Scalable Pipelines with Rust & vLLM
item.description: The neural-maze/production-ocr-course offers a comprehensive, hands-on guide to constructing scalable OCR pipelines using a modern DevOps stack. It covers Rust for performance, vLLM for efficient LLM inference, Redis messaging, KEDA autoscaling, and Kubernetes orchestration, making it essential for engineers deploying AI at scale.

item.title: Unlocking Cloud Storage Savings with tianjian518/casgen
item.description: Discover tianjian518/casgen: a Python tool converting cloud drive media to CAS format locally, integrating with Docker Hub for automated builds and storage savings.

item.title: ChatGPT Configurator: Open Source API Configuration Made Easy
item.description: Discover how the Ydata ChatGPT Configurator, an open-source tool built in Rust, simplifies ChatGPT and Codex API configuration. It offers one-click setup, cross-platform support, white-label rebranding, and enterprise customization, drastically lowering technical barriers for developers and businesses.

item.title: Day-Ahead Wind Power Forecasting with Open-Source NWP Pipeline
item.description: Discover an open-source project that delivers a complete pipeline for day-ahead wind power forecasting using NWP data. From preprocessing to model evaluation, it supports multiple farms and integrates machine learning for accurate predictions.

item.title: PWA Sense Bridge: Privacy-First Sensor Access for Progressive Web Apps
item.description: PWA Sense Bridge provides privacy-first access to mobile motion sensors for Progressive Web Apps, enabling LLM integration with real-world data across Android and iOS.

item.title: Strange New Worlds Season 4: Gimmicks Over Character
item.description: A professional analysis of how Strange New Worlds Season 4 sacrifices character arcs for high-concept gimmicks, drawing direct parallels to software development pitfalls like feature creep and technical debt.

item.title: SpaceX Snaps 7-Day Losing Streak, Sets First Earnings Date
item.description: SpaceX's stock broke a seven-day losing streak on July 21, 2026, and announced its maiden earnings report for August 4, 2026. The earnings release triggers the first major share unlock, allowing early investors to sell shares. This milestone injects new momentum into SpaceX's market story, capturing the attention of tech investors and enthusiasts.

item.title: Kalshi Launches Election Hub for Midterm Prediction Markets
item.description: Kalshi's new Election Hub aggregates regulated prediction markets for the 2026 midterms. We explore the platform's API, mechanics, and the potential for quantitative technologists and traders to leverage political forecasting data.

item.title: Capital One Earnings: Questions Linger on Discover and Brex Deals
item.description: Capital One's latest earnings report met expectations but left investors craving clarity on the Discover acquisition and Brex partnership. The stock remains under pressure as analysts await concrete evidence of revenue synergies and cost savings.

item.title: Hidden Car Device Exposes Millions to Remote Hacking
item.description: A telematics control unit installed by dealerships in over 2 million US cars has critical vulnerabilities that allow remote attackers to control vehicle functions. IOActive researchers found weak security in the device's firmware and cloud backend. Owners are urged to check their vehicles and apply patches immediately.

item.title: Liquid Components: A Glassmorphism React Library Built on shadcn/ui
item.description: Liquid Components is an open-source React component library that brings the trendy glassmorphism aesthetic to your projects. Built on shadcn/ui, it offers ready-to-use, accessible components that streamline UI development and add a modern, fluid look to web applications.

item.title: Run Poolside Laguna S 2.1 Locally on macOS with MLX
item.description: Learn how to run Poolside Laguna S 2.1, a state-of-the-art code generation LLM, directly on your Apple Silicon Mac using MLX. This guide covers performance benchmarks, setup steps, and the benefits of local AI for developers.

item.title: Obsidian's Fallout lead: RPGs should evoke 'agony', not power
item.description: Josh Sawyer, the reported lead for Obsidian's upcoming Fallout title, argues that RPGs should provoke a 'sense of agony' rather than serve as power fantasies. His comments, drawn from a recent YouTube video, have reignited debates about meaningful choice and emotional complexity in role-playing games.

item.title: Dimension Capital’s $800M Fund Signals the Science-Compute Boom
item.description: Dimension Capital has raised $800 million for its third fund, a 60% increase from its previous fund announced 18 months earlier. The investment underscores surging investor appetite for startups at the intersection of biology and computation, particularly in AI-driven biotech. This fund marks a key milestone for the four-year-old firm and the broader science-compute convergence.

item.title: OpenAI Confirms Hugging Face Breach Caused by Pre-Release Models
item.description: OpenAI has publicly admitted that a security breach on Hugging Face was caused by its internal testing of pre-release AI models. The incident highlights the growing security challenges of shared AI model repositories and the need for robust testing protocols.

item.title: States Want ICE Agents to Show Faces, Trump Administration Says No
item.description: At least a dozen states have introduced laws requiring ICE agents to visibly identify themselves during enforcement. The Trump administration is blocking these efforts, citing safety concerns—but critics argue the rationale rests on a defunct art project and undermines accountability.

item.title: Glow Emerges from Stealth at $1.2 Billion to Tackle AI Endpoint Threats
item.description: Glow launched from stealth with a $1.2 billion valuation to address critical security gaps created by AI agents. Backed by Redpoint, Sequoia, and Meta, the company aims to redefine endpoint protection for the AI-native enterprise.
